source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately reporting failed municipal water-quality tests to protect the public

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Examine water sample results in the context of your program to determine whether the tests will be counted as failed tests for compliance. Consider the potential risk of the detected contaminant, its concentration, and any history of non-compliance in the context of the approved operating plan to determine whether corrective action is necessary.
  Note, this is not always a yes/no decision. The system may need to do additional sampling and/or there may be an opportunity for additional treatment to avoid or delay corrective action.
3. Communicate with your Safe Drinking Water Program contact to develop a strategy for dealing with the water-quality issue, and to report it.
  Note, at this stage be prepared to report to the Safe Drinking Water Program that you are doing additional sampling as additional source confirmational testing and/or monitoring of treatment effectiveness.
4. If you decided that you will report the water-quality test as failed, report it using either (or both):
